hypothesis: Broadcom FY2027 company revenue growth of 18.83753816% remains a viable near-term sensitivity anchor even if all non-AI revenue is flat year over year, because the required FY2027 AI semiconductor growth remains below 40% without relying on any unpublished Q4 segment mix or positive non-AI growth assumption.
capital_allocation_importance: The prior AVGO near-term growth anchor depended on carrying forward observed non-AI semiconductor and infrastructure-software growth. This stress removes that favorable assumption and tests whether the relative NVDA/AVGO FCF-IRR comparison still has a plausible one-year AVGO growth input.

decision_rule.USE: Required FY2027 AI semiconductor growth is 30% or less when total non-AI revenue is flat, so the 18.83753816% company-growth anchor does not materially depend on non-AI growth.
decision_rule.CONDITION: Required FY2027 AI semiconductor growth is above 30% but no more than 40% when total non-AI revenue is flat; retain only as a one-year sensitivity anchor, not issuer guidance or a multi-year forecast.
decision_rule.REJECT: Required FY2027 AI semiconductor growth exceeds 40% under flat non-AI revenue, or the result requires an inferred Q4 segment mix.
decision_rule.UNVERIFIED: Issuer-reported FY2026 total or AI semiconductor revenue, or the canonical FY2027 company-growth target, cannot be identified.

method.primary_stress: Hold all non-AI revenue flat at 48.289 billion USD. Do not infer the undisclosed Q4 split between non-AI semiconductor and infrastructure software.
method.required_ai_growth_formula: required AI growth = (FY2027 target company revenue - FY2027 total non-AI revenue) / FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue - 1
method.missing_data_policy: No Q4 segment point estimate is created. OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic/Apollo/Blackstone deployment capacity is not converted from GW or infrastructure transaction value into Broadcom revenue without issuer-disclosed revenue recognition.

results.interpretation: The prior 18.83753816% one-year AVGO company-growth comparator does not require positive non-AI growth: with total non-AI revenue flat, AI semiconductor revenue must grow 34.63000136%. However, a 10% non-AI contraction raises required AI growth to 43.01350830%, so the anchor is not robust to a material non-AI downturn.

prior_three_bucket_full_q4_interval.assumption: Observed Q1-Q3 non-AI semiconductor and software growth carried forward one year.

flat_total_non_ai_stress.assumption: No positive non-AI growth and no Q4 segment-mix estimate.

risk_metrics.reason: This is a point-in-time fundamental forward sensitivity study, not a return-series backtest. Volatility, Sharpe, maximum drawdown and Expected Shortfall would not measure the hypothesis tested here.
material_risks: AI semiconductor growth can decelerate faster than the stress range.
Non-AI semiconductor and infrastructure software can contract simultaneously.
Customer deployment timing can shift revenue between fiscal periods.
Broadcom has net debt in the prior canonical balance-sheet evidence, so equal FCF yield does not imply equal financial risk.

decision.use: Keep 18.83753816% only as a one-year AVGO growth sensitivity input when explicitly paired with the required AI-growth condition.
do_not_use: Do not treat 18.83753816% as Broadcom issuer guidance.
Do not extend it unchanged through FY2028-FY2030.
Do not convert GW deployments or the 35 billion USD AI-infrastructure transaction into Broadcom revenue without disclosed economics.
Do not make a portfolio-weight decision from this growth input alone.

remaining_uncertainty: The one-year comparator survives flat non-AI revenue but fails the <=40% gate once total non-AI revenue falls roughly 6.4% or more. The durability of AI semiconductor growth beyond FY2027 remains unverified because disclosed multi-GW commitments do not specify Broadcom revenue by fiscal year.
next_hypothesis: Broadcom FY2027 company growth of 18.83753816% remains below the 40% required-AI-growth gate when non-AI revenue is stressed using observed historical drawdowns rather than arbitrary -5%/-10% scenarios; if not, the one-year comparator should be rejected for capital-allocation use.
